summary: This is the bakery's cookie template: a domain class that stores one cookie's flavor and can hand back a sentence describing it for the menu. It has no main method, so it is meant to be compiled and used by other classes rather than run on its own.

lines.text: The final modifier locks this field once the object exists, which is why the class has no setFlavor method. A baked chocolate chip cookie cannot be turned into a sugar cookie, and this field reflects that.
Because the flavor can never be changed later, the constructor is the only chance to supply it, so every Cookie object must be created with its flavor already decided.
The this keyword distinguishes the field from the constructor parameter of the same name; assigning a final field inside the constructor is allowed exactly once.
The method returns the description instead of printing it, which lets the calling application decide where the text goes — a menu, a receipt, or the console.
